issues.legal_issue: A person who contributes to a trust at its foundation does not thereby automatically become a joint founder or acquire management rights.
material_facts: Several contributors each provided money when the trust was established, while one contributor provided the largest amount and managed the trust.
The other contributors did not reserve management rights, accepted the trust’s exclusive management by the largest contributor, and did not seek accounts or participate in management.
The contributors later agreed to the appointment of the manager’s grandson as sole managing trustee.
issues.conclusion: The contributors failed to establish that they were joint founders or were entitled to manage the trust in turns in proportion to their contributions.
issues.legal_principle: A contribution at the time a trust is founded is not by itself sufficient to make the contributor a joint founder; that status depends on the surrounding circumstances and the parties’ subsequent conduct. The Court relied on In the Matter of the Endowed Schools Act, 1869 and In the Matter of the St. Leonard, Shoreditch, Parochial Schools, 10 A.C. 304, and Sattikara Venkatarama Chettiar v. O. P. Damodaram Chettiar, 51 M.L.J. 547.

rule.if: trust_founder_status_disputed and contributor_contributed_at_foundation and no_management_rights_reserved and contributors_accepted_exclusive_management and contributors_accepted_successor_as_sole_manager

predicates.trust_founder_status_disputed: A dispute arose in a trust-related proceeding about whether contributors were joint founders.
predicates.contributor_contributed_at_foundation: A person contributed funds when the trust was established.
predicates.no_management_rights_reserved: The contributors did not reserve management rights for themselves when the trust was established.
predicates.contributors_accepted_exclusive_manageme: The contributors accepted that one person would manage the trust exclusively.
predicates.contributors_accepted_successor_as_sole_: The contributors accepted the appointment of a successor as sole managing trustee.

issues.definition: When a trust-founder dispute involves contributions at the trust’s foundation but no reserved management rights and acceptance of exclusive management and a sole successor, the contributors are not established as joint founders.

issues.legal_issue: A person interested in the proper administration of a private trust may bring a civil suit seeking a scheme or a trustee’s removal when mismanagement or breach of trust is alleged.
material_facts: The trust was treated by the parties as a private trust.
The plaintiffs had contributed to the trust and sought a scheme and other relief concerning its administration.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiffs, as contributors interested in proper administration, had a sufficient right to bring a suit seeking relief for mismanagement or breach of trust, even though they were not established as joint founders.
issues.legal_principle: A person interested in the proper administration of a private trust may sue in a civil court for removal of a trustee or settlement of a scheme where breach of trust or mismanagement is alleged. The Court relied on Pramatha Nath Mullick’s case, 52 I.A. 245; Manohar Mookerjee v. Peary Mohan, 24 C.W.N. 478; and Bimal Krishna’s case, 41 C.W.N. 728.

predicates.private_trust_administration_suit: A civil suit concerns the administration of a private trust.
predicates.claimant_interested_in_proper_administra: The claimant has an interest in the proper administration of the trust.
predicates.breach_or_mismanagement_alleged: The claimant alleges breach of trust or mismanagement by the trustee.

issues.definition: A claimant interested in the proper administration of a private trust may bring an administration-relief suit when breach or mismanagement is alleged.

issues.legal_issue: A scheme or removal of a managing trustee is not warranted when the alleged breach of trust or mismanagement is not established.
material_facts: The plaintiffs alleged that pujas, a religious school, and feeding of pupils had been discontinued, and raised other allegations of mismanagement.
Both lower courts found that the allegations of breach of trust and mismanagement were not established.
The Supreme Court found no ground for framing a scheme or removing the managing trustee.
issues.conclusion: No scheme was to be framed and the managing trustee was not to be removed because the alleged breach of trust and mismanagement had not been established.
issues.legal_principle: A scheme for a private trust or removal of its trustee may be sought by an interested person, but the relief depends on breach of trust or mismanagement being established. The Court relied on Pramatha Nath Mullick’s case, 52 I.A. 245; Manohar Mookerjee v. Peary Mohan, 24 C.W.N. 478; and Bimal Krishna’s case, 41 C.W.N. 728.

predicates.private_trust_management_relief_suit: A suit concerning a private trust seeks a management scheme or removal of a trustee.
predicates.breach_or_mismanagement_not_established: The alleged breach of trust or mismanagement is not established.

issues.definition: In a private-trust management-relief suit, if breach or mismanagement is not established, a scheme or trustee removal is not granted.
